title: Chubby Jackson the cheerleader and band ribbing, including a fake MGM screen test
summary: Chubby was the ringleader, Sonny Berman copied him, and Ray Linn and others set up a fake MGM screen test for Pete Candoli.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: We're almost through with that one. That brings to me just to the area that I wanted to see if we could click off on, and there are probably a number of these anecdotes of various sorts.
Well, anyway, another -- at least two categories of stories and anecdotes. See if you can recall something like that.
Well, I think we have to start with the characters themselves.

MR. HERMAN: And some of them were characters. Chubby Jackson was the cheerleader and the ringleader of much of what happened visually in the band and on the stage and so on. He was like the spark plug and could really turn it on. He was
the cheerleader. And whatever he would do on the stand, Sonny Gorman would try to emulate.

Yeah, and Cubby was constantly steaming up different guys, people like Pete, and how some of these things started, just from ribbing and kidding. And all of a sudden another very good trumpet player who was in and out of the band for a short period, he'd been in and out of the band on numerous occasions -- his name is Ray Lind.
And he's now a successful studio player in Southern California. And he became Peter's manager for his theatrical career.
And during one period when they were both -- before they were in my band, they were Tommy Dorsey, and they got Tommy steamed up to get a screen test at MGM for Pete.
But it was a phony. The guy had all the equipment and the lights and the cameras, with probably no film and these sort of things. And they had Pete doing a drawing room scene, wearing golf knickers.

And there were constant ribbing and constant kidding as much as you would find probably in sports football players, baseball players much needling, much kidding around, and if anyone could put anyone else on, and this band put on the
world at the time, so -- and I think that was one of the big -- (End of Side One.)
